findings.description: S-003: the `--add-data "assets:assets"` example is correct for current PyInstaller (the stable docs specify the colon with no platform exception), but PyInstaller before 6.0 used os.pathsep, i.e. ';' on Windows. A sentence noting this would save learners on an older pinned version.
findings.resolution: Fixed in scripts/build_chapter_20.py: added an info callout «Двоеточие в --add-data» noting that current PyInstaller uses a colon on every OS including Windows, that versions before 6.0 used a semicolon on Windows, and that this character is the first thing to check when an older pinned version cannot find the assets. Verified present once in the rebuilt 20-29-upakovka-desktop.html.

evidence.summary: Learning objective and scope: Packages the game into a standalone desktop executable with PyInstaller, covering --onefile, --add-data, the no-cross-compilation rule and hidden imports.

`pyinstaller --onefile --add-data "assets:assets" igra.py` is valid current syntax. -- Confirmed -- pyinstaller.org/en/stable/usage.html specifies source and destination 'separated by a colon (:)' with no platform exception, and documents --onefile as 'Create a one-file bundled executable'.

PyInstaller cannot cross-compile; you must build on each target OS. -- Confirmed verbatim -- 'If you need to distribute your application for more than one OS ... you must install PyInstaller on each platform and bundle your app separately on each.'

Pygame's non-obvious imports may be missed by static analysis and need --hidden-import. -- Confirmed -- --hidden-import is documented as 'Name an import not visible in the code of the script(s)', which is exactly this case.

A working `python igra.py` does not guarantee a working bundle, because asset paths and hidden imports only surface at packaging time. -- Confirmed -- consistent with 20.19's CWD warning, which this section correctly cites.
